plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I bid below my value, I risk losing profitable auctions; if I bid above, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value. Since the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit. My value is $14, so I will bid exactly that amount.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and the price you pay never depends on your own bid except in determining whether you win. Overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of what others do, I will bid exactly my value of $34.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since I only get one round, I should not try to game the system; truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $33, so I will bid exactly that.
